Rules
* 3rd difference: Consider making the additional characteristic stand out more and not stating the existing ones (which are repeated later). For example, simply state:

Pieces have one additional characteristic: Lit/Unlit.

* Please explain the coordinate system.

* Please define what constitutes a 2x2 square. Must its sides be horizontal and vertical, e.g.
ｘ．．．．ｘ
．．．．．．
．ｏｏ．．．
．ｏｏ．．．
．．．．．．
ｘ．．．．ｘ

Or can they also be diagonal, e.g.
ｘ．．．ｏｘ
．．．ｏ．ｏ
．．．．ｏ．
．．．．．．
．．．．．．
ｘ．．．．ｘ

* Please change "Each piece has its 5 characteristics encoded as a 5-bit integer (0 to 31)" to "Each piece has a unique ID from 0 to 31, which is a 5-bit integer encoding its 5 characteristics". The term "ID" is currently used without being explicitly defined.

* Please change "The game is alternating turn-based" to "Players alternate turns" for simplicity.

* "they just placed": Please remove "just", as it unnecessarily implies that only the most recently placed piece is considered for scoring.

Input
* Please add "An integer" before [[myId]], [[pieceToPlace]] and [[N]] (Line 8 only).

Input for one game turn
* Please change "Lines 2 to 7" to "Next 6 lines".

* Please add "space-separated" between "6" and "integers".

* Please change "Line 8" and "Line 9" to "Next line".

Output
* I'm wondering whether it's a good idea to have the game automatically play the final turn for Player 1, instead of requiring Player 1 to output their move. At that point, there's only one remaining piece and one empty cell, so the move is forced. This would make the output format consistently "x y id" throughout the game.

I'll perform play-testing later.

Thanks.

Here’s Quarto 32! An expanded version of the board game Quarto (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarto_%28board_game%29)

Have fun! :)

Thank you for the feedback! I have fully implemented all your suggestions.

I agree with your point regarding the final forced turn. The Referee has been updated to automatically play the very last piece on the final empty cell on behalf of the player. As a result, the required output format for the players is now consistently x y id throughout the entire game!

Glad that helped!

Rules
* Please use <ul> and <li> for the three bullet-point lists instead of manually using "-" and "•".

* Consider formatting some of the important constants that are currently unformatted using <const>.

* Consider adding gameplay diagrams illustrating what does and does not constitute a 2x2 square. (I've already sent you suitable figures via private message on the forum. Feel free to use those or create your own.)

* I initially thought the tie-breaker score was calculated from the final board state, so that if two adjacent pieces sharing characteristics were placed by different players, both players would score points from that adjacency. After looking at the referee code, I realised this isn't how it works. Please clarify how the tie-breaker is scored.

  (I now understand why you used the wording "they just placed", but the word "just" alone isn't enough to convey that scoring happens incrementally on each turn.)

Output
* Please change "2,1" to "(2,1)" for consistency with the coordinate notation used elsewhere.

Viewer
* As the game progresses, it becomes difficult to tell which player placed which pieces. Consider including both the player and the piece ID in the tooltips.

* The viewer displays Player 0's name in blue and Player 1's name in reddish orange, whereas the console uses red for Player 0 and blue for Player 1. Please swap the viewer colours so they match the console.

(By the way, I also noticed that the viewer for Brandubh doesn't distinguish the player colours at all. Player 1's border colour should be changed to blue there as well.)

* When a line of five pieces is formed and the game ends, the final screen only highlights four of them, making the fifth piece appear to disappear. Example: https://www.codingame.com/replay/897714606

* In this replay, where the entire board is filled, pieces also disappear on the final screen: https://www.codingame.com/replay/897731513

Referee
* The referee should reject outputs containing too many parameters (e.g. 4 4 30 60) as invalid. It currently ignores the extra parameters.

* Please add a dedicated error message such as "Non-integer input" when the output contains strings or floating-point values (e.g. A 0 6 or 3.14 0 6). At the moment, the message "For input string" is displayed, which doesn't appear to come from your referee.

Thanks.

Thanks for the new feedback! :) All of these points have been addressed and pushed.

I've already added a clarification to specify that 2x2 squares must have horizontal/vertical sides. I think this should be enough to clear up any ambiguity. Do you think an image is necessary ?

Good catch on the viewer! I fixed a graphical bug that was occasionally causing pieces on the lower half of the board to fade out during the end screen (which is why the 5th piece disappeared in your replay!).
